requirements: Complete the MIT first-year application, including essays, activities and academic history.
Submit the required recommendations and academic records.
Submit SAT or ACT results; review the official test-date policy for your application round.
Check MIT’s English-language testing guidance for your circumstances.

scholarships.name: MIT undergraduate financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: Apply through MIT Student Financial Services. Aid depends on the university’s assessment of financial need and your application documents.

mit.edu.scope: First-year undergraduate applicants; confirm programme-specific rules

requirements: Submit the Common Application and the application fee or a fee-waiver request.
Submit SAT or ACT results.
Provide a school report, counselor recommendation and official academic transcripts.
Provide two academic teacher recommendations and the midyear transcript.
stanford.edu.scope: First-year undergraduate applicants; confirm programme-specific rules

requirements: Complete the Common Application and Harvard questions with the required supporting materials.
Provide school reports, transcripts and teacher recommendations.
Review the current SAT/ACT requirement and the published exceptional-circumstances policy.

scholarships.name: Harvard College need-based aid · 2025–26 onward
scholarships.eligibility: Families earning $100,000 or less with typical assets may qualify for coverage of all billed expenses; those earning $200,000 or less with typical assets may qualify for tuition coverage. The university assesses each family’s financial circumstances.

harvard.edu.scope: First-year undergraduate applicants; confirm programme-specific rules

requirements: Choose a course and check its specific qualifications, subject requirements and admissions tests.
Check the course’s written-work and interview arrangements.
Apply through UCAS using the published Oxford deadline for your entry year.

scholarships.name: Oxford undergraduate bursaries and scholarships · 2027 entry
scholarships.eligibility: Awards depend on residency, household income, course and scholarship-specific conditions. Use the university’s award list to check your eligibility.

scholarships.name: Rhodes Scholarship · Oxford graduate study
scholarships.eligibility: Postgraduate award. Citizenship or residency, age, academic and course-entry criteria vary by constituency; applications in 2026 are for October 2027 entry.

scholarships.name: Oxford graduate scholarships · 2027–28
scholarships.eligibility: Oxford expects more than 1,200 full or partial awards for new graduate students. Eligibility and application routes vary; many awards use the graduate application.

ox.ac.uk.scope: First-year undergraduate applicants; confirm programme-specific rules

requirements: Choose a degree in the official course directory and check its qualification and language requirements.
Use the course-specific admissions route and application period.
Check scholarship and financial-aid conditions separately from admission.

scholarships.name: TUM scholarships and financial support
scholarships.eligibility: Check the university’s listed awards for enrollment, academic, nationality and financial conditions. No general award is guaranteed.

tum.de.scope: Degree-programme applicants; requirements vary by programme and qualification

utoronto.ca.scope: Undergraduate applicants; qualification and programme-specific routes
requirements: Use the admission requirements for your completed or current academic curriculum.
Check the programme’s subject prerequisites and any personal profile or statement of interest.
Provide English-language evidence unless an exemption applies. Check the university’s accepted tests and exemptions.
Use the required-documents and supplemental-application instructions for your applicant category.

uni-ruse.bg.scope: International bachelor’s applicants; confirm your citizenship route
requirements: Prepare the application form, secondary-school diploma and mark sheet. The listed relevant-subject average must be at least 62% of the grading scale maximum.
Provide the document confirming access to higher education and the recognition documents requested by the university.
Review legalization and certified Bulgarian translation requirements for your documents.
Check the medical certificate, passport and photograph requirements. Bulgarian B2 evidence is listed for applicants who will not take the preparatory language course.
The directorate lists 30 September 2026 for the 2026 application process; that cycle has closed. Confirm the next intake directly.

wiut.uz.scope: Undergraduate direct entry or transfer; 2026 instructions are a past-cycle reference
requirements: Check your course for an accepted International Foundation qualification or equivalent, English-language evidence and mathematics competence.
Register in the WIUT Admission System and follow its document instructions.
The published checklist includes English proficiency, secondary education and mathematics certificates; check the requirements for your course.
The page lists 17 August 2026 as the undergraduate deadline. This cycle has closed; ask admissions for the next intake.

ethz.ch.scope: Bachelor’s applicants with non-Swiss matriculation certificates
requirements: Use ETH’s bachelor’s application route for non-Swiss matriculation certificates.
An ETH entrance examination may be required for some qualifications. Check the rules for your exact certificate before applying.
Follow the university’s application instructions and country-specific qualification guidance for your intended intake.
International applicants use the same first-year process as domestic applicants, normally applying at the start of their final year of secondary school.

A Secondary School Report with transcript (about three years of grades plus national exam results such as IB, A Levels or CBSE; predicted grades accepted) must come from the school counselor or another school official.
SAT or ACT scores are required; MIT publishes no cutoff scores.

An English proficiency test is strongly recommended for applicants with fewer than five years of English use; MIT lists minimums of TOEFL 90 (pre-21 Jan 2026 format), IELTS 7, PTE 65, Cambridge English 185 and Duolingo 120.
All application materials must be in English; translations may not be done by the applicant.

scholarships.name: MIT Scholarship (need-based)
scholarships.eligibility: Students who apply for financial aid and complete the CSS Profile are automatically considered; awards are based solely on demonstrated need.

scholarships.name: Need-blind, full-need financial aid for international students
scholarships.eligibility: MIT says it admits international applicants need-blind and meets the full demonstrated need of all admitted students, foreign and domestic.

requirements: Apply through UCAS (up to five choices), with a single personal statement and one academic reference.
Applicants need a qualification accepted as equivalent to A-levels and must meet course-specific subject requirements; most apply with predicted grades.
Some courses require an admissions test (e.g. ESAT, TMUA, UCAT) and some include an interview.
All applicants must meet Imperial's English language requirement, even native speakers; minimum scores are set on a separate English-language page.

scholarships.name: Imperial Inspires Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: For students paying the Overseas tuition rate who apply via UCAS to an eligible full-time undergraduate course in Engineering, Natural Sciences, Medicine or the Business School (2027 entry); £15,000 per year.

scholarships.name: IB Excellence Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Overseas-fee students taking the IB Diploma and applying to undergraduate courses in Engineering, Natural Sciences or the Business School, nominated by departments; £5,000 per year (page describes 2026 entry).

requirements: International students follow the standard first-year application instructions (Common App referenced) and are admitted for fall entry only.
Transcripts and official marks or predictions must be sent by the school, with English translations not made by the applicant.
SAT or ACT scores are required.
English proficiency tests are not required (scores may be self-reported), but fluency in English is a prerequisite.
Teacher recommendations and a counselor recommendation (or another school official if no counselor) are required, translated into English if needed.

scholarships.name: Need-based financial aid for international students
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants must request aid on the admission application; Stanford meets the full demonstrated need of admitted students, but requesting aid is a factor in admission for non-US citizens and aid cannot be requested later.

requirements: Oxford accepts undergraduate applicants worldwide; admission is highly competitive and courses are specialised.
Applicants need an excellent general education, strong English, and eligibility to enter university in their home country.
International applicants pay the higher overseas fee rate and must show the College they have sufficient funding before enrolling.

scholarships.name: Reach Oxford Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For highly able students from developing countries who cannot study for a degree at home for political, financial or facility reasons, who hold an Oxford offer and have outstanding results; not awarded every year.

requirements: Apply via the Common Application plus Harvard's supplement (five short-answer questions); requirements are the same for international and domestic applicants.
A Secondary School Report with transcript, a Midyear Report, and two teacher recommendations from different academic subjects are required.
SAT or ACT is required; in exceptional cases (cost or access barriers) AP, IB, A-level or national exam results/predictions can substitute.
English tests (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo) are not required and do not meet the testing requirement, though scores may be submitted.
Translated documents must be accompanied by the untranslated originals and may not be translated by the applicant.

scholarships.name: Harvard need-based financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: Same aid policy for all applicants regardless of citizenship: admission is made without regard to aid application and Harvard meets each admitted student's demonstrated need, including a travel allowance.

requirements: All applicants, including international students, apply through UCAS using the same process; offers are made on predicted grades supplied by the referee.
A-levels and the IB Diploma are the main qualifications considered, but equivalent national qualifications are accepted.
Most international applicants pay a £60 application fee, waived for some countries.
Selection is based on academic achievement and potential; overseas-fee payers receive no priority. Some courses require admission tests (e.g. UCAT, LNAT, ESAT, TMUA).

scholarships.name: Cambridge Trust (Cambridge Commonwealth, European and International Trust)
scholarships.eligibility: Means-tested awards for overseas students who have received a College offer; applications are only possible after an offer.

scholarships.name: College awards for overseas students
scholarships.eligibility: Some Colleges offer partial financial support to overseas students, with eligibility varying by College.

scholarships.name: International Disabled Students' Fund
scholarships.eligibility: Offer holders and students classed as international for fees can seek help with academic-related disability support costs.

requirements: Applications with non-Swiss school-leaving certificates are submitted through ETH's eApply portal.

Depending on the certificate, admission is granted without exam, or after a reduced (4-subject) or comprehensive (8-subject) entrance examination; certificate-specific rules follow swissuniversities and ETH's country list.
Teaching is mainly in German: a recognised German C1 certificate (or Goethe/ÖSD C2) must be submitted by 31 March unless exempt (e.g. native speakers or German/Austrian school-leaving certificates).

scholarships.name: ETH Scholarship (need-based)
scholarships.eligibility: International Bachelor students may apply via eSTIP after passing the first-year examination (Basisprüfung).

scholarships.name: Solidarity Fund for Foreign Students
scholarships.eligibility: Foreign students with a B permit in their first Bachelor's or Master's programme at ETH; Bachelor students must have passed the first-year exam and meet credit thresholds.

requirements: SAT or ACT scores are required, plus AP or IB scores if taken.
Official transcripts with grades and predicted results must be sent by the school, with English translations of any non-English documents.
Two teacher recommendations: one from a STEM teacher and one from a humanities or social-science teacher.
Non-native English speakers (unless taught primarily in English) must submit an English test: IELTS 7 (7 per section), TOEFL 100 (25 per section; or 5 on post-Jan 2026 format) or Duolingo 130.

scholarships.name: Caltech need-based financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: Caltech meets the full demonstrated need of admitted students, but international admission is need-aware and aid must be requested when applying for admission.

requirements: Apply online through NUS's international application form (S$20 fee), listing up to eight programme choices, with passport copy and results.

Requirements are set per qualification: e.g. IB Diploma, A-Levels, or a completed high-school diploma (such as the American diploma) supported by standardised test scores like SAT/ACT; some national qualifications need minimum grades (e.g. German Abitur 2.0 or better).

Some qualifications must be supplemented with an English test; NUS's list sets minimums such as IELTS Academic 6.5 (overall, reading, writing), PTE Academic 62, C1 Advanced 180 and TOEFL iBT 4.5 (new scale); Law requires higher English (e.g. IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL iBT 100).
Shortlisted applicants to selected programmes may have to attend admission tests and/or interviews.

scholarships.name: NUS International Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Open to citizens of all countries except Singapore who are exceptional international students with outstanding achievements.

scholarships.name: ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For citizens of ASEAN countries other than Singapore, across all undergraduate programmes.

scholarships.name: MOE Tuition Grant
scholarships.eligibility: Awarded competitively to international students to subsidise fees, in return for working for a Singapore entity for three years after graduation; those without it pay non-subsidised fees and cannot get NUS/MOE aid.

requirements: Holders of international qualifications (non-local students, or local students without HKDSE) apply directly to HKU online through the International/Non-JUPAS Admissions Scheme; HKU does not authorise agents.

Minimum requirements depend on your qualification (e.g. GCE/International A-level, IB, SAT/AP) and programme, including subject and English language requirements shown in HKU's admissions-standards tool.
Decisions also weigh interview performance, personal statement, references and other documents; shortlisted applicants may be interviewed between November and January.

For 2027 entry, applications opened 23 Sept 2026 with a first-round deadline of 25 Nov 2026 (noon HKT); later applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and predicted/actual grades must be entered.

scholarships.name: HKU Entrance Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: Merit-based entrance awards for international students that may cover full tuition plus accommodation and a living allowance.

scholarships.name: Belt and Road Scholarship (HKSAR Government Scholarship Fund)
scholarships.eligibility: For nationals of participating Belt and Road countries who show contributions to their community, leadership and commitment to Hong Kong; worth up to full non-local tuition (deadline 31 Jan 2027).

requirements: Apply through NTU's online admissions portal; for AY2027 the window opens 15 Oct 2026 and closes 20 Jan or 19 Mar 2027 depending on qualification.

Qualification rules apply: IB applicants must give NTU direct IBO access to their transcript; UK A-Level applicants should normally have four A2 subjects in one sitting; programme-specific subject requirements apply.

An English test is mandatory for some systems (e.g. Gao Kao, HKDSE, CSAT, GSAT, Vietnam) and where English was not a main subject; minimums include IELTS 6.5 (writing and speaking 6.5), TOEFL iBT 90 (writing/speaking 25), PTE 55, C1 Advanced 170, SAT 1250 or ACT with Writing 30.
Scores must arrive by the application deadline; pending results must be uploaded within 3 days of release.

scholarships.name: Nanyang Global Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Open to all nationalities with outstanding A-Level, IB, polytechnic or Year 12-equivalent results plus strong co-curricular and leadership records; covers subsidised tuition and allowances.

scholarships.name: ASEAN Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For citizens or permanent residents of ASEAN countries other than Singapore with outstanding results and leadership potential, entering a first full-time degree.

scholarships.name: NTU Science and Technology Undergraduate Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For citizens of Asian countries/regions other than Singapore entering a full-time Computing, Engineering or Science degree with outstanding Year 12-equivalent results.

requirements: International students use the same application forms and process as other applicants, listing activities and awards on the Common Application.

A Secondary School Report and transcript are required (any school administrator may complete it if there is no counselor); grades should not be converted to a 4.0 scale, and non-English documents need official translations.
English proficiency scores are optional: applicants may submit any English exam they feel reflects their ability, or none if their application already shows mastery.
Applicants who may ever need need-based aid must apply for it at the same time as applying for admission.

scholarships.name: Need-based and merit-based aid for international first-years
scholarships.eligibility: First-year international applicants can receive need-based and merit aid; UChicago commits to meeting 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students who apply for aid with their admission application.

scholarships.name: Odyssey Scholarship (extended to international students)
scholarships.eligibility: UChicago has extended its Odyssey Scholarship program to international undergraduates, replacing loans with scholarships and funding enrichment opportunities.

requirements: Open to non-Chinese citizens holding a valid foreign passport, generally aged 18–25, who have completed high school; extra nationality conditions apply to applicants of Chinese origin.
Apply online at studyatpku.com ("Written Test Exemption Application for Undergraduate Program"), paying an 800 RMB fee; 2026 entry had two rounds (Dec 2025–Feb 2026 and Jun–Jul 2026).

Applicants submit national or international university-entrance exam scores meeting PKU's score requirements, plus a high-school transcript and Chinese proficiency proof (undergraduate teaching is in Chinese; HSK 6 above 210 is cited for Chinese-taught programmes).
Two recommendation letters, a personal statement, a commitment letter and a self-introduction video are required; shortlisted applicants sit a secondary examination.

scholarships.name: Peking University Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.eligibility: Merit-based award for admitted self-funded full-time international undergraduates with no other scholarship; covers tuition, living allowance and insurance, with no separate application needed.

scholarships.name: Beijing Government Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For international students meeting PKU admission requirements (undergraduates up to age 25) on fee-paying programmes who hold no other Chinese government or PKU scholarship; Types A–C cover tuition and varying extras.

scholarships.name: Chinese Government Scholarship – Bilateral Program (Type A)
scholarships.eligibility: Applicants who pass PKU's initial eligibility check apply through the scholarship authority in their home country; Chinese-taught undergraduate programmes require HSK 6 (210+).

requirements: Applicants must be foreign citizens in good health with a high-school graduation certificate (Chinese citizens with foreign permanent residence are not eligible).
Academic strength is shown through transcripts, national graduation/matriculation exam results and international tests such as SAT, ACT, A-Level, AP or IB.

Chinese proficiency of HSK 5 (each section over 60) is required; HSK 4 is accepted if Level 5 is reached within the first year. Non-native English speakers must also submit an English test score (e.g. TOEFL/IELTS).
Apply via Tsinghua's online application system; applications are reviewed and shortlisted applicants are interviewed (outstanding applicants may receive an offer without interview).

scholarships.name: Chinese Government Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Open to international degree and non-degree students; full awards cover tuition, accommodation, a stipend and insurance, applied for via the local Chinese embassy/consulate with Tsinghua as first choice.

scholarships.name: Beijing Government Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Outstanding international first-year undergraduates can receive full, half or partial tuition awards for the first year, applied for through the online application system.

scholarships.name: Tsinghua University Institutional Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Donor-funded scholarships open to international students; detailed criteria are not stated on the page.

requirements: Apply with the Common App, Coalition Application or QuestBridge; international and domestic applicants follow the same process.
Submit complete official secondary records for every grade level (predicted scores accepted), with certified translations and no third-party recalculation.

English proficiency is required unless English is the native language or the main language of instruction for at least three years; TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic or Duolingo accepted, with competitive benchmarks around TOEFL 100 (or 5 new scale), IELTS 7 and Duolingo 130 (not formal minimums).
Penn uses a comprehensive review with no explicit course requirements or minimum test scores.

scholarships.name: Penn need-based international financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants (non-citizens/non-permanent residents of the US, Canada and Mexico) may request aid when applying; admission is need-aware, and admitted aid recipients get 100% of demonstrated need met for four years.

requirements: Apply via the Common Application plus the Cornell supplement with college/school-specific essays.
An official transcript (with mid-year grades when available) and a school report from the counselor are required.
One counselor recommendation and two teacher recommendations are required.
SAT or ACT scores are required, and international applicants must demonstrate English proficiency through an approved exam or other criteria (minimums are on Cornell's testing policy page).

scholarships.name: Cornell need-based aid for international students
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants who submit the CSS Profile with their admission application (ED 1 Nov 2026 / RD 2 Jan 2027) are considered; admission is need-aware and Cornell meets 100% of admitted students' demonstrated need.

requirements: International applicants complete the same application and requirements as all other applicants and receive the same whole-person review.
SAT or ACT scores are required; international leaving exams and English tests do not satisfy this.

An English test (TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge English, Duolingo or InitialView) is required unless the applicant has completed at least two years of secondary school taught in English; no minimum scores are listed.
All materials, including transcripts and recommendations, must be in English, with certified (not self-made) translations.

scholarships.name: Yale need-based financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: Yale admits international students need-blind and meets 100% of demonstrated need with the same aid as domestic students, including housing, meals and travel allowances.

requirements: Applicants must complete secondary school with a certificate that qualifies them for university entry in their country; IGCSE/O-levels alone are not enough (e.g. A-levels with at least three exams or the IB Diploma are needed).
Grades must be reported exactly as shown on the school record, without conversion; extra national exam results (e.g. French Baccalaureate, ATAR) are submitted after admission.
English proficiency must be shown by 31 January: TOEFL 90 (4.5 new scale), IELTS 6.5 or Duolingo 115, or alternatives such as AP English 3+, IB English, or 3+ years of English-medium schooling.
Optional InitialView interview materials may be sent by 30 November but cannot replace an English test score.

scholarships.name: Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: All applicants, including international first-year and transfer students, are automatically considered through a holistic review of top applicants.

scholarships.name: Robinson International Scholars Program
scholarships.eligibility: Need-based award for admitted international students who are refugees or stateless people from Sub-Saharan Africa or other developing nations (or graduated from school there), on top of the Regents' and Chancellor's Scholarship.

scholarships.name: International Leaders Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Need-based award for admitted international students with academic excellence and leadership, with priority for Peruvian residents.

requirements: Non-local applicants needing a Hong Kong student visa apply through the International Students Admissions Scheme and must meet general, language and programme-specific requirements.

General minimums include IB Diploma 30/45, GCE/International A-level 3AL (or 2AL+2AS), or a US diploma with SAT 1190 / ACT 24 plus two AP tests at grade 3; other national qualifications have their own minimums.
English minimums include IELTS Academic 6.0 overall, TOEFL iBT 80 (or 4.5 on the post-Jan 2026 scale), SAT EBRW 590 or ACT ELA 23, among other accepted qualifications.
Admission is competitive; meeting minimums does not guarantee an offer.

scholarships.name: CUHK Admission Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: New non-local undergraduates with excellent academic or non-academic records are identified automatically (no application); awards range from HK$5,000 to full tuition, some with allowances.

scholarships.name: HKSAR Government Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: CUHK nominates outstanding first-year undergraduates, including non-local students, to the Education Bureau; no application required.

scholarships.name: Belt and Road Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For outstanding new students from Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Mongolia, Myanmar and Thailand, with a separate award for other Belt and Road countries.

requirements: Apply online via the UNSW Applicant Portal (directly or through an agent; UAC International is also mentioned); places are allocated on academic merit and capacity.

Each degree has an indicative international ATAR (2027 table); predicted IB, A-Level, CBSE and similar results are accepted for full offers if at least 2 points above the requirement, and SAT/AP/ACT results can earn early offers.
A new International Admissions Diversity Pathway gives passport holders from eligible countries 5 extra points toward their international ATAR (minimum 75).
Applicants must meet UNSW's English requirements (listed per degree); conditional offers can be met with English results or UNSW College's UEEC course.

scholarships.name: International Student Award
scholarships.eligibility: Citizens of eligible countries starting in 2026 or 2027 receive a 20% contribution toward tuition fees each year; combinable with other awards.

scholarships.name: International Scientia Coursework Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For international students with high academic achievement plus leadership and extracurricular involvement; application required (full tuition or $20,000 per year).

scholarships.name: Australia's Global University Award
scholarships.eligibility: High-achieving international applicants are considered automatically for a one-off $10,000 tuition payment.

requirements: Apply with the Common Application or the Coalition Application on Scoir; there is no separate international application.
Submit official academic records for the equivalent of US grades 9–11 plus any O-level, A-level or IB results, with verified English translations.

Standardized testing is required, and an English test (TOEFL, IELTS, Duolingo or Cambridge) is recommended for non-native speakers without three recent years of English-medium schooling; no minimums listed.
All international applicants must submit the Certification of Finances form via the applicant portal, or the application is incomplete.

scholarships.name: Need-based financial aid for international students
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants who indicate aid on their application and submit the CSS Profile (or JHU's own form) are considered; admission is need-aware and Hopkins meets 100% of demonstrated need without loans.

scholarships.name: Merit scholarships for international citizens
scholarships.eligibility: All applicants are automatically considered for a small number of merit scholarships offered to international citizens each year.

requirements: The online application form opens in November; first-year Bachelor places are capped at 3,000 and EU/EFTA/UK and IB holders are ranked by general average.

EU/EFTA certificates need at least 12 years of schooling, six of seven required subjects including maths and physics at the highest level, and at least 80% in maths, physics and overall; the IB Diploma needs HL maths, physics and a third science, 38/42 points and 6/7 in maths and physics.
Holders of certificates from other countries may be admitted only to the preparatory Cours de mathématiques spéciales (if meeting equivalent criteria) or via the EPFL entrance exam.
Bachelor programmes require French at CEFR B2 (C1 highly recommended); applicants who did not study French in upper secondary school must prove their level.

scholarships.name: EPFL social scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Need-based, last-resort support for students who have completed the first-year cycle and at least one year at EPFL and face an unexpected change in financial circumstances; full funding must be secured before enrolling.

requirements: Applicants need a recognised university entrance qualification; foreign qualifications can be assessed via uni-assist, and applications are submitted through TUM's online application.
Most Bachelor's programmes use an aptitude assessment whose procedure depends on the programme.
German-taught programmes require proof of German, e.g. DSH-2, TestDaF 4 in all sections, DSD II (B2), telc C1 Hochschule or Goethe/ÖSD C2.
For English-taught programmes, English is either checked in the aptitude assessment or shown with TOEFL iBT 88, IELTS Academic 6.5, PTE 65 or Cambridge CAE/CPE (A–C).

scholarships.name: TUM Deutschlandstipendium
scholarships.eligibility: Open to admitted or enrolled TUM students including internationals, with an entrance-qualification grade of at least 2.40; recipients must be resident in Germany with a German bank account (next round summer 2027).

scholarships.name: TUM Scholarship for International Students
scholarships.eligibility: Bavarian-funded merit-and-need award (€500–€1,800 per semester) for students ineligible for BAföG due to nationality, from the 3rd semester of a Bachelor's.

requirements: Transcripts are read in the context of the home education system and should include internal grades and external exam results (IGCSE, A-Level, IB, national exams), with predicted or achieved results sent as available.
A School Report from the counselor (or principal/dean), a Midyear Report where applicable, and a graded written paper in English are required.

An English test (TOEFL, IELTS Academic, Duolingo or PTE Academic) is required unless English is the native language or the applicant had at least three years of English-medium secondary school; no minimums listed.
Forms in other languages must be officially translated (school staff may translate).

scholarships.name: Princeton need-based financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: Admission is need-blind and international students receive the same need-based, grant-only aid policy as US students.

requirements: Apply directly from the course page or through an authorised agent (Year 12/IB students studying in Australia apply via UAC), paying a processing fee.

Applicants must meet academic entry requirements (recognised overseas qualifications and entry scores) and the Australian Government's Genuine Student requirement; a Taylors College preparation programme is an option for others.

Submit official transcripts/certificates, proof of English proficiency, passport and any programme-specific items (e.g. personal statement or portfolio), with accredited translations of non-English documents.

scholarships.name: Sydney International Undergraduate Academic Excellence Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For international students applying for a first full-time single undergraduate degree with no prior tertiary study; covers 100% of tuition for up to 4 years, subject to a 65 average.

scholarships.name: Vice-Chancellor's International Scholarships Scheme
scholarships.eligibility: International students with an unconditional offer to a bachelor's or coursework master's degree are automatically considered on merit; one-off awards up to $60,000.

scholarships.name: Sydney International Student Award
scholarships.eligibility: Citizens of eligible countries admitted to a full-time degree starting in 2027 receive a 20% tuition reduction, with a personal statement required.

requirements: Applicants must be non-Chinese citizens with foreign passports who have finished high school, are healthy and have no criminal record; extra nationality rules apply to children of Chinese citizens.
Apply online at istudent.fudan.edu.cn/apply with an 800 RMB fee; applicants sit the CSCA assessment (Maths in English for this programme) and attend an interview.
Documents include the high-school diploma and transcript, CSCA score report, two English recommendation letters, proof of funds and a no-criminal-record certificate.
English test needed unless schooled in English: minimums TOEFL 90, IELTS 6.5, Duolingo 110 or PTE Academic 61.

scholarships.name: Fudan University International Students' Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Awarded by the university to excellent applicants based on academic performance and admission evaluation results.

requirements: Apply online through McGill's applicant portal (opens 1 October; application deadline 15 January, supporting documents by 1 March).

Upload the high-school transcript (with mid-year results), any GCSE/IGCSE/O-Level or MYP results, and predicted or final results; e.g. IB applicants need at least 5 in each subject, with typical program ranges such as 33–36 (Arts) or 35–39 (Science) out of 42.

Proof of English proficiency is required unless the applicant attended school for at least four years in a country where English is the primary language; test results are due by the supporting-documents deadline.
Some programs or scholarship/aid applicants need extra items such as French proficiency, CASPer, recommendation letters or a personal statement.

scholarships.name: McGill Entrance Scholarship Program
scholarships.eligibility: Merit-based awards for newly admitted first-year, first-degree full-time undergraduates, including US and international students; the renewable Major award requires a separate application by 21 January.

scholarships.name: Need-based financial aid (loans and bursaries)
scholarships.eligibility: Undergraduates from Canada, the US and abroad can apply for need-based bursaries and loans based on financial need or hardship.

requirements: Applicants with a French or European baccalaureate, and EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, apply through the national Parcoursup platform.

Non-EU applicants in 'Études en France' countries with a foreign diploma apply via Parcoursup (CPES), the EEF/Campus France portal (e.g. Sustainability Sciences, International BSc in AI, Dauphine-PSL) or the I-BE³ platform, depending on the programme.
Non-EU applicants outside EEF countries use the DAP procedure for some programmes, Parcoursup for CPES, or programme-specific platforms; admitted students must obtain a student visa.
The PSL Classes Internationales preparatory year requires three years of transcripts, a one-page personal statement and a CV.

scholarships.name: Dauphine-PSL Hardship Assistance
scholarships.eligibility: Enrolled Dauphine-PSL students facing financial difficulties can apply via MyDauphine; no nationality restriction is stated.

scholarships.name: Tuition Scholarship – Dauphine London Bachelor's
scholarships.eligibility: Academic- and need-based support for students enrolled in Dauphine's London bachelor's programme.

requirements: Apply through the Ontario Universities' Application Centre (OUAC), then use U of T's applicant portal to upload documents and complete forms; the process is the same for international and Canadian applicants.
Requirements vary by program; all applicants need senior-level English and any program prerequisites, assessed within the curriculum they are completing.
Applicants must meet U of T's English language requirement (minimum scores are on a separate page); some programs also require supplemental applications.

scholarships.name: Lester B. Pearson International Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: International students in their final year of secondary school (or graduated no earlier than June 2026) who are nominated by their school and start in Sept 2027; covers tuition, books, fees and residence for four years.

scholarships.name: President's Scholars of Excellence Program
scholarships.eligibility: About 150 top direct-entry first-year applicants, domestic and international, are considered automatically.

scholarships.name: Arts & Science Global Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Selected outstanding international students admitted to Arts & Science, with financial need possibly considered; covers international tuition, incidental and UHIP fees for up to four years.

requirements: Australian Year 12, IB Diploma and NZ NCEA students apply via UAC International; all others apply directly through ANU's online portal (AUD$150 fee, up to three preferences).
Applicants must meet the minimum indicative entry scores for their program plus any additional selection criteria; conditional offers may be made while documents are outstanding.
Evidence of meeting ANU's English language requirements is required (minimum scores on a separate page).
Semester 1, 2027 applications close 15 December 2026; OSHC health cover is mandatory for student-visa holders.

scholarships.name: ANU Chancellor's International Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Commencing overseas students with an offer to an eligible program are assessed automatically on merit for a 25% or 50% tuition reduction depending on region.

scholarships.name: International Merit Award
scholarships.eligibility: International undergraduates with a Selection Rank of 85 (or equivalent) or higher, from countries not eligible for the Vice-Chancellor's award, are considered automatically for a 20–50% tuition reduction (2026 intake).

requirements: Apply through UCAS; requirements are set as specific qualifications and grades per course (no UCAS tariff points), with referees supplying predicted grades.
Accepted qualifications include three A-levels, the IB Diploma (e.g. 36 points / 18 at HL ≈ AAA), and US routes combining APs with SAT/ACT or at least five APs.

English requirements are banded by course: e.g. Band B IELTS 7.0 (6.5 each skill) or TOEFL iBT 100; Band D IELTS 6.5 (6.0 each skill) or TOEFL iBT 92, with exemptions for some majority-English-speaking nationals.
Applicants who don't meet standard requirements can consider King's International Foundation Programme.

scholarships.name: King's International Hardship Fund
scholarships.eligibility: Limited fund for enrolled international and EU students who face financial difficulty despite having had adequate funding; awards up to £6,000.

requirements: Holders of international qualifications (e.g. SAT/ACT/AP, A-Level/IAL, IB, French/European Baccalaureate) must meet general, programme-specific and English language requirements.

Apply via the HKUST Online Application System (HKD600 fee), choosing up to two options; for 2027 entry the priority deadline is 25 Nov 2026, with rolling review afterwards and final close 30 Jun 2027.

Submit a personal statement, school reports from Grade 10 onward, proof of English proficiency (IELTS, TOEFL, Duolingo, PTE or qualifications such as IB/A-Level), public exam results and at least one academic referee; IB/A-Level counsellors provide predicted grades.
Interviews may be arranged and are required by some programmes.

scholarships.name: Global Learners Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: All undergraduate applicants from underrepresented nationalities are automatically considered for a renewable full tuition waiver.

scholarships.name: University Admissions Scholarships (merit)
scholarships.eligibility: All applicants are automatically considered on academic merit and non-academic achievements; no separate application.

scholarships.name: Future Leaders Award
scholarships.eligibility: Application-based non-academic scholarship listed for non-local applicants; a separate application is required (detailed criteria on a linked page).

requirements: Full-time undergraduate applications go through UCAS; selection is made by colleges/schools and applicants are compared with others of the same fee status.
Each degree sets its own subject and grade requirements; a wide range of international qualifications is accepted, and some subjects use interviews, tests or portfolios.
All applicants must show English competency; scores vary by degree, IELTS/TOEFL must be under two years old, and C1 Advanced/C2 Proficiency require 176 overall with 162 per component.
An unsuitable personal statement is cited as a reason applications can be unsuccessful.

scholarships.name: Edinburgh Global Undergraduate Mathematics Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: For international applicants to mathematics with outstanding academic performance.

scholarships.name: Global Talent Fund BIG Scholarships
scholarships.eligibility: For students from anywhere in the world who have won a medal at an international Olympiad.

scholarships.name: Asylum Seeker Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For applicants seeking asylum who are most in need; covers tuition fees and living costs (two awards for 2026-27).

requirements: Apply through UCAS (from 1 Sept 2026 for 2027 entry); the academic reference must be complete before UCAS accepts the application.
Equal-consideration deadline is 13 January 2027 (15 October 2026 for Medicine and Dentistry); final UCAS deadline 30 June 2027.
Applicants must meet general and course-specific entry requirements; many overseas qualifications are accepted (see country-specific pages), with foundation courses as an alternative route.
English requirements are usually equivalent to IELTS 6.0–7.0 depending on the course (5.5 for foundation courses).

scholarships.name: Global Futures Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Partial merit-based awards for residents of listed countries holding an offer for a full-time on-campus course starting September 2027; criteria vary by region.

scholarships.name: Humanitarian Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Supports people forced to flee their homes due to armed conflict and persecution; no awards currently open (2027/28 details may be posted later).

requirements: Graduates of overseas high schools apply to the traditional (Japanese-taught) undergraduate programmes through the Special Screening Tests; detailed guidelines are published only in Japanese.
A high level of Japanese proficiency is required because most courses are taught in Japanese.
English-taught degree options are PEAK (four-year, at Komaba) and the Global Science Course, a 3rd-year transfer programme for students with at least two years of study at a university outside Japan.

scholarships.name: Japanese Government (MEXT) Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Applied for via Japanese embassy recommendation (or university recommendation for some categories); undergraduates first take a one-year preparatory course and may not be placed at UTokyo.

scholarships.name: Global Science Course support
scholarships.eligibility: All admitted GSC transfer students receive a monthly JPY 150,000 scholarship and fully supported accommodation.

requirements: Open to foreign-passport holders who have completed (or will complete) high school; apply through the Common App, then complete steps in the SJTU Portal (Early Action 1 Nov 2026, Regular 31 Mar 2027).
A CSCA score with Mathematics is required (can be submitted by 30 June 2027 after pre-admission), plus one of SAT/ACT, A-Level (Maths A+) or IB (Maths HL 5+/SL 7+) or another national exam.
Non-native English speakers need TOEFL iBT 90 (4.5 new scale), IELTS 6.0 or Duolingo 120; all students must reach HSK 4 to graduate.
Submit transcripts from every high school, two recommended English recommendation letters, and a financial statement of at least CNY 100,000.

scholarships.name: International Chinese Language Teachers Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: For pre-admitted students to the Bachelor's in International Chinese Language Education with HSK 5 (200+) and HSKK intermediate (60+).

scholarships.name: Chinese Government Scholarship / SJTU Scholarship
scholarships.eligibility: Listed as available to international students on SJTU's scholarship page; eligibility details are not given there.

requirements: Apply via the Common Application or Coalition Application on Scoir (QuestBridge for finalists) plus Columbia-specific questions; the process is largely the same regardless of citizenship.

A Secondary School Report (transcript, counselor recommendation, school profile, midyear report) and two teacher recommendations are required; non-English documents need official translations with originals.
Any curriculum is accepted; external exam results (A Level, IB, AP, national exams) must be submitted if required to graduate.

Applicants must be comfortable with rapid, idiomatic spoken English (separate English proficiency requirements); InitialView/Vericant videos are optional. Columbia is test-optional for 2026-27 and reinstates testing from the 2027-28 cycle.

scholarships.name: Columbia need-based international financial aid
scholarships.eligibility: International applicants who request aid with their application are reviewed need-aware; Columbia meets 100% of demonstrated need for admitted students with grants and work-study, no loans.
